volumes.item: **Leads per month:** ~120 (normal months); variable based on weather.

evidence.quote: Depends on the weather. A normal month is about 120 leads.
About forty-five estimates a month.
The close rate. Get it from 30% to 35%.
What's an average job worth? Around$14,000 for a full replacement.
And no estimate with zero. Follow up. That number should be zero, not 19.

pains.item: No system for follow-ups; estimators forget to call back customers. | 19 out of 45 estimates receive no follow-up. Potential loss of $40,000+/month if more close.

evidence.quote: So when a customer calls back and asks for their estimator, Tasha has no idea what was already said.

pains.item: Estimator fatigue leads to missed follow-ups (writing estimates late at night). | Follow-ups are often the last thing on estimators' minds after a long day.

evidence.quote: Tell me more about how the estimators work day to day. They write the estimate at night from home, usually after eight. So by the time they're done they're tired, and following up on old estimates is the last thing on their mind.

pains.item: Lack of documentation in Job Nimbus regarding follow-up calls. | Tasha cannot recall what was discussed; customers may be left hanging until next week.

evidence.quote: Do they log their follow up calls anywhere? They're supposed to make a note in Job Nimbus.

pains.item: Scheduling adjuster meetings is chaotic ("nightmare"). | Eight or nine messages required to set one meeting; adjusters change times frequently.

evidence.quote: Scheduling that is a nightmare. Dasha goes back and forth with the homeowner and the adjuster by phone and text. Sometimes eight or nine messages to set one meeting.

pains.item: Estimator missing an adjuster meeting. | Adjuster writes claim without estimator present, missing damage details; requires filing a supplement that delays work by another two years.

evidence.quote: What does it cost you when the estimator misses an adjuster meeting? The adjuster writes the claim without us there and he usually misses damage. Then we have to file a supplement, which can take another two years.

outcome.item: **Goal:** Every estimate receives a follow-up on Day 2, Day 5, and Day 10 until the customer says yes or no.

evidence.quote: Every estimate gets a follow up on day two, day five, and day ten until the customer says yes or no, and the estimator gets a heads up when the customer replies, so he can call it.

outcome.item: **Measure:** Increase close rate from 30% to 35%. Eliminate estimates with zero follow-ups (target: 0).

summary_markdown:
**Company and People**

*   **Company Name:** Ridgeline Roofing
    *   **What it does:** Residential roofing, including full replacements, repairs, and insurance claim management.
*   **People Mentioned:**
    *   **Owner:** (Speaker)
    *   **Tasha:** Office Coordinator
    *   **Jake:** Lead Estimator
    *   **Estimators:** Three estimators in total (one is Jake; the other two are unnamed).
    *   **Production Manager:** Manages production, ordering materials, scheduling crew, and permits.

**Workflow Steps**

| **Step** | **Who** | **Tool** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Leads enter system | System | Job Nimbus (CRM) |
| Lead books inspection | Tasha (Office Coordinator) | Phone |
| Estimator visits site | Estimator | Job Nimbus (for building estimate) |
| Estimate sent to customer | Estimator | Email (PDF) |
| Follow-up on estimate | Estimator (supposedly) | Job Nimbus (supposed notes) |
| Insurance adjuster meeting scheduled | Tasha | Tasha's phone, Google Calendar, Email |
| Work execution and sign-off | Production Manager/Crew | N/A |

**Volumes and Timing**

*   **Leads per month:** ~120 (normal months); variable based on weather.
*   **Estimates sent per month:** ~45.
*   **Close rate:** ~30%.
*   **Average job value:** ~$14,000 (full replacement).
*   **Estimates with zero follow-up:** 19 out of 45.
*   **Potential revenue loss estimate:** Over $40,000/month if three more estimates from the "zero follow-up" group close.
*   **Adjuster meetings per month:** ~20 (normal months).

**Tools and Systems**

*   Job Nimbus (CRM)
*   Phone (Tasha's phone)
*   Google Calendar (for estimators)
*   Email
*   ABC Supply (ordering materials)

**Pain Points**

| **Pain** | **Cost or impact** |
| --- | --- |
| No system for follow-ups; estimators forget to call back customers. | 19 out of 45 estimates receive no follow-up. Potential loss of $40,000+/month if more close. |
| Estimator fatigue leads to missed follow-ups (writing estimates late at night). | Follow-ups are often the last thing on estimators' minds after a long day. |
| Lack of documentation in Job Nimbus regarding follow-up calls. | Tasha cannot recall what was discussed; customers may be left hanging until next week. |
| Scheduling adjuster meetings is chaotic ("nightmare"). | Eight or nine messages required to set one meeting; adjusters change times frequently. |
| Estimator missing an adjuster meeting. | Adjuster writes claim without estimator present, missing damage details; requires filing a supplement that delays work by another two years. |

**Desired Outcome and Measure**

*   **Goal:** Every estimate receives a follow-up on Day 2, Day 5, and Day 10 until the customer says yes or no.
*   **Measure:** Increase close rate from 30% to 35%. Eliminate estimates with zero follow-ups (target: 0).

**Decision Makers**

*   **Owner:** Signs off on the solution.
*   **Stakeholders for review:** Tasha (Office Coordinator) and Jake (Lead Estimator) must see the plan first as they will implement it.

**Next Steps**

| **Owner** | **Action** | **When** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tasha | Pull a list of last quarter's estimates from Job Nimbus with the status of each one. | This week |
| Owner | Put together a one-page plan for estimate follow-up (single lane/trial on new estimates only). | After receiving Tasha's list (implied next Tuesday morning) |
